title: add-oncall-context-snapshotter-and-automated-mitigation-actions
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: on-call responders often need a reproducible snapshot of service state and a set of low-risk automated mitigations to reduce time-to-action during incidents. This PR introduces two coordinated features: 1) a lightweight OnCall Context Snapshotter that captures service-level telemetry, recent traces, scaled-down heap/profile samples and the last 100 lines of relevant logs into a compressed snapshot and uploads it to an internal S3 bucket; 2) a set of configurable Automated Mitigation Actions that can be invoked from Slack (via incident-bot message actions) or from the web console; mitigations include safe restart (graceful restart with drain), temporary autoscale-up (short TTL), cache invalidation for a specific keyspace, and a controlled circuit-breaker toggle. Safety gates and a risk classifier are included to require human confirmation for high-risk actions (e.g., DB schema-level operations).
Key points and behavior: - Snapshotter runs with a 6s sampling window by default and attaches metadata (alert id, SLO hit, topology tag). Snapshots are encrypted with KMS and TTL-ed after 30 days. - Mitigation actions are executed by the Bot Worker in a dedicated sandbox account with limited IAM roles; actions emit trace events and an audit log entry. - Integration with slo-toolkit: alerts with SLO breach score > 0.8 will surface a recommended mitigation and the snapshot link in the Slack alert message. - Config: new incident-bot config block incident.snapshot and incident.mitigations with per-environment allowlists, cooldowns, and risk thresholds. - CLI: new incidentctl snapshot create and incidentctl mitigation simulate for on-call engineers to reproduce actions locally.
Backwards compatibility: mitigations are opt-in via allowlists; default behavior is read-only.
Checklist: - [x] snapshot capture + upload - [x] Slack action + confirm modal - [x] mitigation executor with dry-run support - [x] KMS encryption + access controls - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] SLO recommendation hook - [x] doc snippets and runbook guidance (docs/incident-bot/snapshot-and-mitigations.md)
Related issues: Linear ENG-4127 tracks the end-to-end UX; SUP-334 notes a customer incident that motivated the snapshot TTL change.
Commits summary: - Add snapshotter core (pkg/snapshotter): captures CPU/mem profiles, logs, traces, metadata and uploads compressed artifacts - Add mitigation executor (pkg/mitigations): dry-run and execute paths, IAM sandbox integration, audit events - Slack + console UX (internal/slack/actions.go, web/ui/mitigations.tsx): actions, confirm modal, action history - Integration with slo-toolkit scoring (pkg/slohook): recommend mitigation and attach snapshot link - incidentctl CLI helpers and simulate mode - Tests: unit tests and an integration harness stubbed to local S3 and KMS - Docs: initial runbook and ops guidance
Files changed (high-level): - pkg/snapshotter/snapshotter.go (new) - pkg/mitigations/executor.go (new) - internal/slack/actions.go (modified) - web/ui/mitigations.tsx (new) - cmd/incidentctl/snapshot.go (new) - pkg/slohook/handler.go (modified) - scripts/integration/local_s3_stub.go (new) - docs/incident-bot/snapshot-and-mitigations.md (new) - internal/audit/auditlog.go (modified to accept mitigation events)
Tests and CI: initial CI run failed on integration tests due to a race in the local S3 stub (flaky temp file cleanup); fixed by ensuring atomic renames and retry backoff (see commit 3c9f2a4). Final CI: pass (unit+integration matrix, e2e smoke on linux).
Security review: included a short threat model; mitigation executor runs in sandbox account and requires a two-person approval for DB schema-affecting actions.
Performance: snapshotting adds ~120ms median latency to the incident-bot handler when triggered synchronously; default behavior in Slack is async (background job) to avoid impacting alerting flows.
Rollout plan: feature gated behind incident.snapshot.enabled and mitigation allowlists; staged rollout to SRE teams, then production-wide after 2 weeks of monitoring.
Rollback: feature flags and IAM revoke path.
Release notes: "OnCall Context Snapshotter and optional Automated Mitigation Actions: captures contextual snapshots and provides opt-in mitigation actions from Slack and console. Disabled by default; requires config to enable."
Merge: squash-merged to main, merge commit 3f2b8d1.
Documentation: docs/incident-bot/snapshot-and-mitigations.md contains setup, example Slack flows, and operator runbook.
Breaking change: false

review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Love the snapshot idea, left a few inline nits around context tagging and TTL semantics. Please ensure no PII captured in logs.
Aisha Patel (author): Good catches, Marco. Adjusted log scrubbing to strip email-like patterns and added a config allowlist to opt into verbose captures.
Chen Li: Mitigation executor looks solid but we should add rate limiting and a global cooldown; otherwise an alert storm could trigger repeated autoscale actions.
Aisha Patel: Added cooldown config and a default 5m backoff for scale actions. Also implemented per-action rate limits.
Evan Brooks: We need clearer audit entries for any mitigation that changes infra state; confirm we emit a trace/span tied to the alert id.
Aisha Patel: Audit entries now include alert id, mitigation id, executor user (bot) and optional approver id. Trace spans are instrumented in executor.
Evan Brooks: Approved with suggestion to monitor the 120ms median hit; perhaps switch Slack flow to async by default (implemented).
ci_log_snippets: e2e smoke: linux ok, macOS matrix skipped for now
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in OnCall Context Snapshotter and Automated Mitigation Actions. Snapshots are encrypted and TTL-ed; mitigations are sandboxed and require confirmation for high-risk operations. Enabled via config allowlists.
notes_for_ops: Enable incident.snapshot.enabled=false by default. To enable: set incident.snapshot.enabled=true in env/config and populate incident.mitigations.allowlist with team ids. Ensure KMS key and S3 bucket exist and review IAM sandbox roles. Monitor audit logs and mitigation action counts in the first 48h.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental high-impact actions executed automatically. Mitigation: default opt-in allowlists, two-person approval for DB-affecting actions, sandbox IAM roles, audit trail and TTL on snapshots.
qa_notes: Run 'make test-integration' with local_s3 stub. Use incidentctl simulate to validate mitigation flows without executing changes. Verify audit entries appear in internal audit service.
human_readable_summary: Adds on-call snapshot captures and opt-in mitigation actions surfaced in Slack and the console. Focused on reducing time-to-diagnosis and providing safe, auditable automations for common recoveries. Gated and audited.
